purpose: Bind the exact bytes of both blind reader packages -- twelve files, six per reader -- BEFORE the Coordinator composes them at TASK-20260916-a8e5b5. Each reader owns disjoint joints and neither read the other's directory, so composition is the first point at which the two verdicts meet; hash-binding them first is what makes the composition auditable against what the readers actually filed rather than against what the Coordinator remembers them filing.
commit_sha_note: Null in the receipt as written, because a file cannot contain the hash of the commit that contains it. The value is recorded in this batch's dispatch_queue.json under the archive block of TASK-20260916-92128f, together with this receipt's own sha256, and research_dispatch.py verifies both.
binding_mode_reason: content_first, deliberately unlike this batch's opening archive, which binds content_at_commit. A reader's filed report is IMMUTABLE: it must read identically at HEAD forever, and if it does not, something edited a producer's artifact after filing. content_first is the mode that catches that, because it verifies the declared hashes against HEAD rather than against this archive's own tree. The opening archive cannot use it, because the control plane it binds contains the goal head and this queue, both of which legitimately move afterwards. Two modes in one batch, each matched to whether its subject is allowed to change.
path_sha256_note: TWELVE entries and not thirteen: the receipt's own hash is in the queue, not here. Six per reader, which is the widened declared set -- the first attempt at this round declared three per reader, produced six, and lost the three undeclared ones with the machine (CORR-20260921-942a62).

the_source_artifacts_were_ALREADY_COMMIT.what_happened: Each reader's declared set was committed by tools/producer_landing.py the moment that reader returned, before this archive task ran: c31504e97 for TASK-20260916-9da6e0 and c0a107514 for TASK-20260916-64a93b. This archive's own commit therefore stages ONLY the receipt, and does not create the twelve files it binds.
the_source_artifacts_were_ALREADY_COMMIT.why_that_is_deliberate_and_not_a_shortcu: This is the remedy recorded in CORR-20260921-942a62. The historical pattern -- producer writes to the working tree, Coordinator archive commits it later -- leaves every deliverable uncommitted for the length of the gap between production and archival, and on 2026-09-21 that gap swallowed an entire round: two reader packages and an executor run, none of which had ever been committed when the machine went away. Landing closes the gap to seconds.
the_source_artifacts_were_ALREADY_COMMIT.what_it_does_NOT_change: Ownership is unchanged: exactly one archival task (this one) owns these twelve artifacts, declared through archive.source_task_ids and checked by the archive_artifact_coverage_complete gate. The producer still did not commit -- both readers were instructed not to run git add, commit, or push, and neither did; the Coordinator ran the landing. And the binding is unchanged, because content_first verifies the declared hashes against HEAD rather than against a changed-path set, so it asks the question this archive actually means: are these still the bytes the readers filed.
the_source_artifacts_were_ALREADY_COMMIT.the_cost_stated_plainly: A landed-then-archived artifact is committed twice as far as history is concerned -- once for durability, once for the receipt that binds it -- so the archive commit is no longer the place a reader looks to find out when an artifact first existed. Read the landing commit for that. What is bought is that the artifact exists in the repository before anything can lose it.
